issues.legal_issue: A permanent injunction may be granted on established possession without determining title where the suit seeks only protection of possession and the circumstances establish that the defendant is not in possession.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought a permanent injunction to protect possession and did not seek a declaration of title.
The plaintiff’s possession was found established and was supported by the defendant’s admission.
The defendant had previously brought a claim for declaration and recovery of possession of the same property, and that claim and the ensuing appeal were dismissed.
The plaintiff’s plaint did not set out a title dispute requiring a declaration.
issues.conclusion: The injunction suit was maintainable and could be decreed on the basis of the plaintiff’s admitted and established possession without deciding the validity of the plaintiff’s title documents.
issues.legal_principle: Possession is good against all but the true owner, and even a person in established possession may obtain an injunction. The Court relied on Nair Service Society Ltd. v. K.C. Alexander and the principle affirmed in Parry v. Clissold. A bare injunction suit may be decided on possession where the pleadings and circumstances do not require adjudication of title; the Court distinguished Nagar Palika, Jind v. Jagat Singh, Advocate, where title and possession were denied and the title document was not produced.

rule.if: proceeding_is_bare_possession_injunction and plaintiff_possession_is_established and defendant_admitted_plaintiff_possession and defendant_prior_claim_to_possession_failed

predicates.proceeding_is_bare_possession_injunction: The plaintiff brought a proceeding seeking to restrain interference with possession rather than seeking a declaration of title.
predicates.plaintiff_possession_is_established: The evidence in the proceeding established that the plaintiff was in possession of the property.
predicates.defendant_admitted_plaintiff_possession: The defendant’s own evidence or statements acknowledged the plaintiff’s possession.
predicates.defendant_prior_claim_to_possession_fail: The defendant had previously sought possession of the same property and failed to obtain it.

issues.definition: When a proceeding seeks only protection of possession, the plaintiff’s possession is established and admitted, and the defendant’s earlier claim to possession failed, an injunction may be granted without deciding title.

issues.legal_issue: The requirement that a plaintiff succeed on the strength of the plaintiff’s own title applies to suits seeking declaration of title and possession, not to a suit seeking only an injunction based on possession.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought an injunction and did not seek a declaration of title or possession.
The plaintiff’s possession was established on the evidence, including the defendant’s admission and the outcome of the defendant’s prior litigation concerning the property.
The plaintiff relied on a sale deed, but the High Court’s decision to grant an injunction did not depend on adjudicating the validity of the title documents.
issues.conclusion: The rule requiring a plaintiff to establish title independently of the weakness of the defendant’s case did not govern this injunction suit.
issues.legal_principle: In suits for declaration of title and possession, the plaintiff must establish the plaintiff’s own title irrespective of whether the defendant proves a competing case; the Court relied on Jagdish Prasad Patel v. Shivnath and Union of India v. Vasavi Cooperative Housing Society Ltd. That principle did not control a suit seeking only an injunction based on possession. The Court distinguished Nagar Palika, Jind v. Jagat Singh, Advocate, which involved a disputed title claim in an injunction suit and a missing title document.

predicates.proceeding_is_bare_possession_injunction: The plaintiff brought a proceeding seeking an injunction to protect possession and did not seek a declaration of title and possession.

issues.definition: When the proceeding seeks only an injunction to protect possession rather than a declaration of title and possession, the rule requiring proof of the plaintiff’s own title does not govern.
